chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs13078086
predictions: There will be no reproducible allele-specific TF binding effect attributable to this variant and no variant-dependent regulatory effect on PYDC2 or CCDC50.
Any colorectal cancer association, if one exists, is not established by the supplied evidence and could reflect another variant or mechanism.
falsified_if: The variant is shown to cause reproducible allele-specific TF binding and a linked, variant-dependent effect on a regulatory element and target gene.

chains.title: Low-confidence CTCF–nearby element–PYDC2 model: alt binding

links.claim: This speculative model proposes that CTCF binds the alt G allele more strongly than the ref T allele. The supplied evidence does not support that direction: no CTCF peak overlaps the variant, and no CTCF QBiC-SELEX result is supplied. The CTCF signal reported for the nearby cCRE is not evidence of occupancy at the variant.
The variant might influence dELS cCRE EH38E2269392, but it is 42 bp away and does not overlap the cCRE.
PYDC2 is a speculative target because it is relatively close to the variant and is listed near the cCRE; no evidence establishes that the cCRE regulates PYDC2.
HCT 116 is the expression context proposed for this model, but no variant-overlapping CTCF peak or HCT 116-specific activity of the nearby cCRE is shown.
A PYDC2 regulatory effect contributing to colorectal cancer is only a hypothesis; the supplied evidence does not connect this variant or PYDC2 to the disease.

predictions: A direct binding assay using the variant sequence would show greater CTCF binding to G than T.
If the proposed regulatory chain is correct, editing T to G in HCT 116 would produce a reproducible change in PYDC2 expression, dependent on the nearby element.
falsified_if: A direct allele-specific binding assay finds no CTCF binding difference or finds greater binding to T.
Precise T-to-G editing produces no reproducible PYDC2 expression change, or the change is unaffected by perturbation of the nearby element.
